To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cell-autonomous osmosensitivity of magnocellular vasopressin (VP) neurons depends on the TRPV1 channel, and that the sensitivity of these neurons to osmotically induced mechanical stimulation is modulated by the actin cytoskeleton.
The osmosensitivity of magnocellular vasopressin neurones depends on a variant of the TRPV1 cation channel, and that this osmosensitivity can be modulated by the neurotransmitter angiotensin-II.

vasopressin neuronal osmosensitivity depends on TRPV1 channels and that the sensitivity of these channels depends on the density of the underlying actin cytoskeleton, which in turn can be modulated by angiotensin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular mechanisms that regulate osmosensitivity of hypothalamic vasopressin cells, a process that is fundamental for body water homeostasis.
how osmosensation is integrated into the regulation of body fluid homeostatis and the mechanisms underlying this regulation.
how the vasopressin system senses changes in plasma osmolality and how it is modulated by other factors.

the sensitivity of vasopressins neurons depends on the actin density in their plasma membrane.

osmosensation of the vasopressin neuron is dependent on a TRPV1 variant, and is mediated by a process where the cell autonomously senses the osmotic gradient across the plasma membrane by a mechanical process that depends on actin filament density.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
osmosensation in vasopressesin neurons is mediated by a mechanosensitive TRPV1 variant that is regulated by actin density.
the osmosensory gain is regulated by the density of the actin cytoskeleton, and that the angiotensin system is involved in the modulation of this process.
vasopressin neuron osmosensation is a dynamic and flexible process that can be modified in response to physiological or pathological stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
osmosensory cells are not passive sensors but rather dynamic elements of the body fluid homeostatic control system.
